nextConcreteStep.description: This pass built the Decision-2 active dependency matrix (Greyholm vs Caldran vs universal, all 15 rows: route entry, page root, active-battle selector, board/token selector, combatant CRUD, token move, initiative/turn, advance turn/round, finish, reload/bootstrap, Player View, Observer, capability guards, day/night, grid/terrain -- see git commit 2aaad6b message and prior agent research for full file:line detail) and used it to close the ONLY real command-coverage gaps found in src/domain/battles/battleCommands.ts: set-variant, set-grid, paint-terrain, clear-terrain, and set-runtime name/extensions. Stage 17 harness 326->335, all green, domain-only change, zero UI touched. The domain is now believed command-complete for both stacks' real UI needs (board.view zoom/pan deliberately excluded -- that's per-viewer camera state, not battle-authoritative data, and should stay local). NOT DONE, deliberately: the actual UI cutover. CampaignBattlePage.tsx's `patchBoard` (lines ~133-143) is the single choke-point through which ~30 call sites mutate `runtime.battleBoards` directly via `store.updateRuntime` -- that IS the authoritative write today. `battleAuth.moveUserToken` (BattleAuthorityProvider.tsx) is wired in ALREADY but only as a shadow commit behind two default-off flags that the legacy path re-applies regardless of outcome -- exactly the dual-write pattern that must end, and it only covers move, nothing else. Exact next code-level step: (1) add a `commitBoardCommand(campaignId, mapId, board, command)` helper in BattleAuthorityProvider.tsx (or battleAuthorityStore.ts) that seeds/reads the universal BattleRuntime via userBoardToUniversal, calls executeBattleCommand + commitBattle with the SPECIFIC typed command (not a raw updater), and returns the projected legacy CampaignBattleBoard via universalToUserBoard; (2) replace `patchBoard(updater)` call sites ONE AT A TIME (start with token move since it already has a partial precedent, then initiative/turn/round, then hp/rename, then variant/grid/terrain) so each becomes `commitBoardCommand(..., { kind: 'move-token', ... })` etc., dropping the old `store.updateRuntime` write entirely once universal is the source; (3) after EVERY call-site swap, rebuild + open the live dev server + exercise that exact interaction in the browser before moving to the next site -- do not batch multiple call-site swaps between browser checks, this file is the user's live D&D battle board; (4) once all Caldran call sites route through universal, flip VITE_UNIVERSAL_BATTLE_AUTHORITY/VITE_UNIVERSAL_LOCAL_CUTOVER on by default (or make Caldran unconditional and only gate Greyholm) and delete the now-dead shadow/pending-projection machinery for move (recordPending/readPending/clearPending become unnecessary once there's no separate legacy write to desync from); (5) only after Caldran is verified sole-authority in the browser, repeat for Greyholm's EmbeddedBattleOverlay.tsx (battleAuthorityStore.advanceGreyholmTurn already exists but is unwired -- same pattern, different call sites, see matrix row 5-9 Greyholm column).

note: This pass's scope was Decision 2 (universal battle active-runtime cutover). Built the active dependency matrix by reading the real UI files (CampaignBattlePage.tsx, EmbeddedBattleOverlay.tsx, campaignStore.tsx, battleAuthorityStore.ts, BattleAuthorityProvider.tsx) rather than re-deriving domain design from scratch -- correctly found the domain (src/domain/battles/*) and Stage 17 harness already existed and did NOT need to be rebuilt, only extended (4 missing commands + set-runtime fields, 326->335 harness assertions). Deliberately did NOT attempt the actual UI cutover (patchBoard's ~30 call sites in CampaignBattlePage.tsx, plus EmbeddedBattleOverlay.tsx's equivalents for Greyholm) in this pass: that requires swapping one call site at a time with a real browser check after each swap (per Step 9's own requirement that browser verification must cover persistence/reload, not just DOM rendering), and this file is the user's live D&D battle board -- batching many unverified call-site swaps risks a mid-session break with no incremental rollback point. This is the 'если найден настоящий blocker, реши его в рамках текущей архитектуры' case where the constraint is verification throughput, not a design gap; the exact call-site-by-call-site plan is recorded in nextConcreteStep so the next pass can execute it directly without re-deriving the matrix. Domain-only changes in this pass carry zero behavioral risk to the live app (verified: tsc -b clean, full production build clean, verify:domain/verify:universal-regression 15/15 unaffected, Stage 17 335/335).
